coverage.main: Reviewed the complete 31-page arXiv 2007.08489v2 (8 December 2020), including all experimental sections, appendices A-G and numerical tables. Visually checked pp. 1-2, 16 and 22 for task definition, main results, pretraining clean accuracies and the adversarial-example illustration.
coverage.supplement: Downloaded and read the separately linked 16-page NeurIPS supplement (printed pp. 14-29), including its additional ten-run figures in F.1 and all numerical tables. Visually checked PDF pp. 6 and 8 (printed pp. 19 and 21). It overlaps the arXiv appendices but has different figure numbering: supplemental Figures 11-12 are ten-run downstream transfer-learning comparisons, and Figures 13-17 correspond to arXiv Figures 11-15.
coverage.excluded_results: All original empirical transfer results concern representation/weight reuse across tasks, not attacked-input transfer between models. Sections 2-3, Table 1 and Figures 2-3: fixed-feature/full-network clean downstream classification over twelve datasets. Section 3, Figure 4 and Appendix C/Figure 9: detection and segmentation AP after backbone initialization. Sections 4.1-4.3, Table 2, Figures 5-7 and Appendices F/G: accuracy, architecture/width and image-resolution ablations of transfer learning. Section 4.4/Figure 8 and Appendix F: stylized-ImageNet/texture invariance comparisons. Appendix A/Tables 3-5: clean pretraining accuracy, training budgets and dataset sizes. Appendix B/Table 6: downstream learning from L-infinity-robust pretraining. Appendix G/Tables 8-11: numerical downstream-learning results. Figure 1 reproduces feature visualization/inversion from prior work; Appendix E/Figure 10 illustrates a single-model Inception-v3 attack without a source-target transfer evaluation. Appendix D is related work.

f1.locator: Sections 1-4; Appendix A.1, Tables 3-4; Appendix G
f1.evidence: The paper reports ImageNet and downstream clean accuracies, but its source/target terminology refers to transfer-learning tasks rather than models in an attack-transfer experiment. Do not treat these as a yes for attack-pair reporting or a no for insufficient reporting.

f2.evidence: Downstream classification uses learned features or fine-tuned weights. There is no located attack-transfer denominator whose clean-correct restriction can be coded; this is not a missing-denominator judgment.

f3.evidence: No original cross-model attack-success population is evaluated. Adversarial training and a single-model attack illustration do not define a transfer denominator conditioned on source attack success.

f4.evidence: Dataset sizes, repeated-run clean accuracies and downstream AP concern different outcomes. No in-scope transfer rate exists for count reconstruction; no reporting deficiency is inferred.

f5.evidence: Numerical L2 and L-infinity radii are explicitly reported for robust pretraining, but these are not budgets of a cross-model attack-transfer evaluation. Preserve this affirmative training detail without converting it into an in-scope yes or no.

f6.locator: Abstract; Appendix A.4; author Hugging Face model card
f6.evidence: The authors release pretrained models for transfer learning. The dated GitHub access failure does not prove artifact absence, and the accessible model collection does not supply an original attack-transfer configuration where none is reported. Do not count this as non-recomputable attack-transfer research.

bounds_exclusion.locator: Sections 2-4; Appendices A-G, including supplemental F.1
bounds_exclusion.reason: No original cross-model attack-transfer rate was located. ImageNet pretraining clean error and downstream task accuracy differ in tasks, labels, populations and trained predictors; they are not the clean and attacked probabilities required by the survey identity. No numerical bound is calculated.

limitations: Retain this paper in the frozen top-80 corpus. The non-applicability reason must be reported separately from unresolved reporting when summarizing conditioning or recomputability.

All six categorical values remain within the frozen yes/no/unclear vocabulary; the adopted amendment's reason metadata identifies non-applicability rather than adding a category or silently dropping the paper.
This is a non-blind scope/evidence audit, not a blind reliability observation or validation of the paper's transfer-learning results.
